# A chip field wraps its triggers onto a row of their own

Sub of #21329. Owned by @neo-opus-ada for the Engine 14 cut (Mon 23 Nov), so no curated labels: the `form-field-chip` tile in neomjs/pages#109 crops this field.

## Context

Found on PR #21369 (#21366), whose operator-requested 7.5 px text inset makes each glyph-less chip wider. Measured on `dev` `28fed2adc6` in devmode, `examples/form/field/chip` on `neo-theme-light`, setting the field's `width` (the inspector's own control) through `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs`:

| Field width | Row 1 | Row 2 | Field height |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300 px (default) | value list 175 px, input 80 px (its minimum), clear and dropdown triggers | none | 36 px |
| 270 px | value list 175 px, input 81 px | the clear trigger, then the dropdown trigger, at the row's start | 65 px |

At #21369's head the default 300 px example renders the second case: `rework-field-dark-after.png` on `ada/21366-evidence` (`1c1cf5c35a`).

## The Problem

The chip field's input row wraps (#21349 AC-5 makes the outline span it), and its triggers wrap with it. Once the chips and the input fill the first row, the dropdown trigger moves to the start of a row of its own. It reads as a stray glyph under the chips, and the field grows by a row with nothing to type into.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/form/field/Text.mjs` `afterSetTriggers()` renders the input wrapper as `[...startTriggers, input, ...endTriggers]`.
- `src/form/field/Chip.mjs` `insertValueListVdom()` splices the value list in before the input, and its `afterSetTriggers()` override re-runs it after every trigger rebuild.
- `resources/css/src/form/field/Chip.css`: `.neo-chipfield .neo-input-wrapper` is one flex row with `flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px`, and the input is `flex: 1 1 80px; min-width: 80px`. Value list, input and triggers are siblings in that row, so a trigger wraps like a chip.
- No stylesheet selects `.neo-input-wrapper > …`; `Picker` aligns its picker to the input wrapper by id. `Text#getInputEl()` finds the input by a deep `VDomUtil.find`, so nesting it does not break the lookup.

Design authority: `align_='end'` (`src/form/field/trigger/Base.mjs`) puts a trigger at the field's end. #21349 AC-5 lets the chip field's input row wrap; no record places triggers in that flow.

## The Fix

- `insertValueListVdom()` groups the value list and the input in one flow node, `{cls: ['neo-chipfield-flow'], cn: [valueListReference, input], id: <field id>__flow}`, where the input sat, instead of splicing the list before it. It runs after every trigger rebuild, so the grouping survives trigger changes.
- `resources/css/src/form/field/Chip.css`: the input wrapper stops wrapping, and `.neo-chipfield-flow` takes `display: flex; flex: 1 1 auto; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px; min-width: 0`. The triggers keep their places at the wrapper's start and end, centered on the field's height by the wrapper's existing `align-items: center`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Once the chips and the input fill the first row, the clear and dropdown triggers stay at the field's end, beside the wrapped chips and input, instead of starting a row of their own.
- [ ] AC-2: A chip field whose chips and input fit one row renders as before (one row, 36 px).
- [ ] AC-3: Adding or removing a trigger keeps the grouping: the value list stays before the input, inside the flow node.
- [ ] AC-4: Typing, Backspace removing the last chip, and the picker's alignment work as before.
- [ ] AC-5: A browser spec narrows the field until the chips and the input fill the row, and reads the triggers' edge: red on base, green at head.
- [ ] AC-6: Post-merge: the `form-field-chip` tile shows the triggers at the field's end.

## Out of Scope

- The chip's fill and text spacing (#21366).
- Where a text field shows its error (#21324, Out of Scope).

## Avoided Traps

- Absolutely positioned triggers over an end padding on the wrapper: the padding would have to track how many triggers show.
- Shrinking the chip text inset until the default example fits: it fixes one width and leaves the wrap at every other.

## Related

- Parent: #21329. Siblings: #21349 (the wrapping input row, AC-5), #21366 and PR #21369 (the text inset that pushes the default example over).
